findings.name: exotic-source
findings.title: resolved from a local directory instead of the npm registry
findings.explanation: bun.lock resolves npm:bun-types@workspace:packages/bun-types from a local directory (workspace:packages/bun-types) rather than from the npm registry. None of the registry's protections apply to it: the release cannot be yanked, advisories are not matched against it, and there is no publisher, provenance or download history to compare with the previous version. The version number the lockfile records is what the manifest in that directory says, not a version anyone published. A path entry is a local directory: nothing was fetched, so there is nothing to check. A workspace member looks exactly like this. This is reported at info rather than at the level the policy sets for exotic-source, because that level is meant for a version fetched from a git repository or a URL, which is what a pull request can repoint under review, and not for an entry a monorepo or a bundling package manager writes for itself. An allow entry for exotic-source with a package glob takes it out of the report altogether.
